messages:
jamie_sre: heads up — multiple hosted inference customers in eu-central2 reporting 502s and high tail latency. spike started ~10:12 UTC, error rate rising. putting initial traces here.

maria_support: ACME escalation: ~50% of requests return 502 gateway errors. customer timestamped failures ~10:14-10:20 UTC. sending repro curl now.

kevin_oncall: are there any deploys or config pushes in that window?

jamie_sre: no deploys. infra metrics: p50 token latency steady, p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~1.2s. overall 5xx went from 0.2% -> 4.8% for eu-central2 frontends. retransmit rate and TCP reorders up on egress links.

ryan_netops: running quick network checks. seeing short AS path withdraws from transit peer AS64512 toward our eu-central2 egress for a few prefixes. also microbursts + reorders on egress. posting snippets:
```
10:13:41 BGP: WITHDRAW prefix 203.0.113.0/24 from peer 203.0.113.45 (AS64512)
10:13:42 TCP: dupack spikes -> retransmit series for flows to 203.0.113.0/24
```

jamie_sre: can you paste a tcpdump/traceroute sample? need to correlate to app logs.

ryan_netops: tcpdump shows repeated dup ACKs + out-of-order segments around 10:13:40-10:14:05: 
```
10:13:40.123 IP hostA > hostB: seq 1000 ack 0
10:13:40.125 IP hostA > hostB: seq 2000 ack 0 (retransmit)
10:13:40.128 IP hostB > hostA: ack 1000 (dup-ack)
```
small bursts of loss and reorder causing connection stalls and HTTP gateway timeouts.

caroline_prod: I'm starting traffic diversion to eu-west1 for noisy prefixes as a canary to reduce customer impact. enabling fallback for new requests and slowly shifting 20% -> 60% over 15m.

maria_support: passing repro step to ACME and others:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
they also sent sample request ids: r-cc9a... (10:15 UTC).

kevin_oncall: i've enabled the router fallback policy to prefer alternate transit peers for eu-central2 for the affected prefixes. watching error rate.

infra-bot: ALERT: transit-peer-AS64512 path-withdraw events=6 within 3m for eu-central2-egress.

ryan_netops: confirmed provider-side BGP instability + link microbursts causing reorder and small packet loss (0.3-0.8%). impact: TCP stalls -> HTTP 502s at our gateway. recommended next step: open provider escalation and request persistent path validation / optics check.

jamie_sre: mitigation notes: 1) reroute traffic to eu-west1 for affected customers; 2) enable more aggressive TCP keepalive and shorter retransmit timers on gateway workers temporarily; 3) reduce per-host concurrency on proxy to limit head-of-line delays; 4) ask netops to push provider ticket. log these for postmortem.

maria_support: customers notified. ACME confirms errors dropped from ~50% -> ~3% after reroute. they asked for ETA; told them netops has provider ticket and we'll follow up. :thumbsup:

kevin_oncall: creating incident page and assigning P1 to netops for provider follow-up and routing stability. will add graphs and attach tcpdump/traceroute.

ryan_netops: raised ticket with transit provider (ref TP-2029-EC2). attaching full BGP/optics dump to incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/2951234567 (internal link).

jamie_sre: thanks all. capture repro request ids, RTT/retransmit histograms, and config changes. we'll start postmortem template after stabilization.

maria_support: closing customer-facing escalations once ACME and others confirm. will reopen if they see new errors.

kevin_oncall: final status (10:53 UTC): error rate down to baseline ~0.3%, p95 latency returning to normal. leaving P1 open for provider remediation until they confirm optical fix.
